definition: A VPC is a logically isolated virtual network.
An interface endpoint provides network interfaces through which a consumer reaches an endpoint service.
An endpoint service is a provider's service made available to consumers through VPC endpoints.
An endpoint policy controls which principals can use a VPC endpoint to access a service.
DNS translates domain names into IP addresses used to reach services.
A CIDR block represents a range of IP addresses.
A security group controls traffic allowed to and from associated resources.
